plain_description.what: Earlier two-way split tests were re-run against a stricter 'deflated' random baseline for the structure certificate. A negative control cut the data along its longest axis. No calls were made.
plain_description.why: It checks whether the certificate can tell real two-category structure apart from data that is merely stretched in one direction.
plain_description.information: If the deflated baseline certified real splits but not the axis-cut controls, it would be a usable certificate for data-driven splits. Result: done, valid. The deflated baseline certified the real splits and the meaningless axis cuts alike (5 of 5 each). Its verdicts follow high-variance directions whether or not discrete structure is there. So it does not discriminate, and it is not a usable certificate for this purpose. The hypothesis it was meant to test was neither refuted nor supported.
